answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a nontrivial stake before it may bid, then slash that stake when independent, randomly assigned counterparties confirm provable fraud, such as failing to deliver escrowed work. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence for free: every new account needs capital, and detection destroys part of it. The rule should judge evidence, not whether a profile sounds hollow or writes a sonnet; a kernel of reputation can help route reviews, but must not replace proof.
